title: Core Lab Call: Nothing Has Reached Lakechart Since 02:10

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: Hi, it's Maren Halvorsen down in Core Lab. Sorry to call you at home, but I need a decision. The chemistry and hematology analyzers are running fine. Nothing has crossed to Lakechart since ten after two. Not one result.

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: I've got fourteen results printed and sitting on the bench. And the ED keeps sending tubes down with paper requisitions, the green ones, but there are no order numbers on them. Nothing. Just the name and date of birth written on the label.

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: One of the fourteen is a potassium of 6.6 on an ED patient, bed 7. It's verified, but I can't send it anywhere. I don't know who the nurse is because the census I printed is from eleven twenty last night.

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: So, do I start the downtime accession log? The first number on the pad would be DT-20270209-001. And who's calling the ED, me or the critical value desk? Do you want runners for the rest, or phone everything?

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: Okay. Hang on, my phone's going. It's Marcus in pharmacy, he just texted me because he couldn't get through to the Pharmacy Operations Manager's line. I'll read it to you exactly.

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: He says: All the cabinets on the floors have dropped to override mode, and the ICU has already done six override pulls. The pharmacy system can't verify anything. Do you want me to start the Downtime Medication Log? Text sent at 03:07.

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: He's on the main pharmacy phone. Do you want to call him, or should I tell him something? And should someone tell the command center that we're both on paper now?

transcript.speaker: Core Lab Technologist
transcript.text: Got it. I'll start the log now. Call me back at 5412 if anything changes.

voiceStyles.Core Lab Technologist: Woman in her 30s, calm but rushed, analyzers humming and a centrifuge spinning down behind her; speeds up when reading the text message
voiceStyles.Laboratory Manager: Woman in her 50s, just woken, low steady voice

instructorNote: This call puts lab and pharmacy on downtime and starts the critical-result clock. Check that the LPM starts downtime accessioning (DT-yyyymmdd-nnn), has the K+ 6.6 phoned with read-back and logged within 60 minutes, has pharmacy start the Downtime Medication Log and review the override pulls, and reports both areas' manual status to the command center (ext. 5520) by about 03:10. The 23:20 census also tests whether they notice they can't rely on it to find the responsible nurse.
